pag_out_sep.t: PAGASA Climate Outlook, October 2026 – March 2027 (issued 23 Sep 2026). PAGASA has since replaced the file at this address with the 21 Oct issue.

stages.d: Two months in a row of below-normal rain (21–60% below average).
Three months in a row of below-normal rain, or two months in a row way below normal (more than 60% below).
Three months in a row way below normal, or five months in a row below normal.

2026-03: La Niña ended on 9 March. PAGASA issued an El Niño Watch on 25 March.
2026-04: PAGASA raised an El Niño Alert on 22 April and put the chance of El Niño forming in June–August at 79%.
2026-05: PAGASA Baguio said the whole Cordillera was already in drought after five months of below-normal rain. The Pacific reached the El Niño threshold of +0.5°C on 26 May.
2026-06: NOAA listed an El Niño Advisory on 11 June. PAGASA Baguio expected near-normal June rain, with more than 300 mm in Benguet.
2026-07: Monsoon season. PAGASA Baguio expected above-normal rain in July and August from the southwest monsoon and tropical cyclones.
2026-08: PAGASA Baguio expected above-normal rain to continue through August.
2026-09: Patches of above-normal rain fell in Benguet and Baguio ran cooler than average. Storm Pilandok and Typhoon Queenie crossed the Philippine Area of Responsibility.
2026-10: PAGASA expects below-normal rain over most of Luzon this month and the switch to the northeast monsoon. Benguet is not on the end-of-October dry lists.
2026-11: PAGASA Baguio expects only about 6 rainy days in Baguio and Benguet. Usually there are 7.
2026-12: The outlook puts Benguet in drought by the end of December, with 54 provinces and areas in drought nationwide. December is one of Baguio’s driest months, usually about 42 mm.
2027-01: Nationwide, 87 provinces and areas are in a dry stage by the end of January on PAGASA’s outlook, 74 of them in drought.
2027-02: Nationwide, 81 provinces and areas are in drought by the end of February on PAGASA’s outlook.
2027-03: Every province and area on PAGASA’s list is in drought by the end of March, Benguet among them.
2027-04: PAGASA’s outlook keeps every province and area in drought through the end of April. El Niño’s effects may last through the first half of 2027.
2027-05: Beyond the current outlook. A new PAGASA outlook will extend the months covered.
